deals.whyRanked: Cheapest verified fare of the five at $167–177 RT nonstop, and Everglades National Park is under 2 hours south.
deals.soloWhy: Las Olas Blvd and the beachfront promenade are walkable and easy to explore alone, though most of the rest of the metro is car-dependent.

highlights: Las Olas Boulevard shops and sidewalk cafes
Fort Lauderdale Beach promenade at sunrise
Riverwalk and the NSU Art Museum
Everglades airboat tour or a ranger-led walk on the Anhinga Trail
Bonnet House Museum & Gardens
itinerary: Day 1 — Beach promenade walk at sunrise, Las Olas Blvd for lunch and gallery-hopping, dinner on the Riverwalk.
Day 2 — Rent a car for the day, drive to Everglades NP's Ernest Coe entrance, walk the Anhinga Trail, add an airboat tour near Sawgrass if time allows.
Day 3 — Bonnet House Museum & Gardens or a paddleboard morning on the New River, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown/Las Olas and the beach are walkable to each other via the Riverwalk, but a rental car is worth it for the Everglades day — return it same-day to skip resort parking fees.
guide.stayArea: Las Olas or Fort Lauderdale Beach — both walkable to restaurants and within a short ride of each other.

deals.whyRanked: A legitimate $188–219 RT floor for September travel — no park boost, but it's the second-cheapest verified fare of the five.
deals.soloWhy: Downtown Tampa and Ybor City have walkable pockets, but the metro is spread out and mostly needs a car or rideshare between neighborhoods.

highlights: Tampa Riverwalk and Curtis Hixon Park
Ybor City's cigar-factory history and nightlife
The Florida Aquarium
Bayshore Boulevard (world's longest continuous sidewalk) for a run or walk
Armature Works food hall
itinerary: Day 1 — Riverwalk from Curtis Hixon Park to the Florida Aquarium, dinner at Armature Works.
Day 2 — Ybor City walking tour and cigar-factory history, evening on 7th Avenue.
Day 3 — Bayshore Boulevard walk or bike, Hyde Park Village shopping, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The Riverwalk and downtown/Ybor corridor are walkable via the free TECO streetcar; a car or rideshare helps for anything past Hyde Park.
guide.stayArea: Downtown/Channelside or Hyde Park — both close to the Riverwalk and streetcar line.

deals.travelWindow: Sep 5 – Nov 14, cheapest one-stop from $203, nonstop from ~$247
deals.whyRanked: $203 RT (one-stop) to one of the most walkable solo-friendly cities in the country, with a national park unit 30–45 minutes away.
deals.soloWhy: The French Quarter and Garden District are dense, walkable, and full of solo-friendly bars and jazz clubs, with streetcars covering the rest.

highlights: French Quarter architecture and Jackson Square
Frenchmen Street live jazz (no cover at most bars)
St. Charles streetcar through the Garden District
Barataria Preserve boardwalk trail — alligators and cypress swamp
National WWII Museum
itinerary: Day 1 — French Quarter walk, Jackson Square, Cafe du Monde, Frenchmen Street for live jazz at night.
Day 2 — St. Charles streetcar through the Garden District, National WWII Museum in the afternoon.
Day 3 — Drive or rideshare to Barataria Preserve for the boardwalk trail, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: French Quarter, CBD, and Garden District are walkable or a short streetcar ride apart; a rideshare or rental car is easiest for the Barataria Preserve trip.
guide.stayArea: French Quarter (lively, walkable) or the Garden District (quieter, still streetcar-connected).

deals.travelWindow: Aug 20 – Nov 4, currently a low-fare window per fare trackers
deals.whyRanked: $222–226 RT nonstop across multiple airlines right now, and Rocky Mountain NP is 90 minutes up the road.
deals.soloWhy: LoDo and RiNo are walkable and full of solo diners at the bar, the A Line train runs straight from the airport downtown, and Bear Lake's easy trails make for a low-stakes solo hiking day.

highlights: RiNo (River North) street art and brewery row
Larimer Square for dinner and people-watching
Denver Botanic Gardens
Bear Lake Road in Rocky Mountain NP — easy trails, no permit off-season
Meow Wolf's Convergence Station for something weird and solo-friendly
itinerary: Day 1 — Land, A Line into Union Station, wander LoDo and Larimer Square, dinner and a beer flight in RiNo.
Day 2 — Rent a car, drive to Rocky Mountain NP via Estes Park, hike Bear Lake to Nymph and Dream Lake (easy, ~2 mi round trip), sunset over Lake Estes.
Day 3 — Denver Botanic Gardens or Meow Wolf, browse REI's flagship store, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: Downtown is walkable and the A Line light rail covers the airport-to-LoDo run with no car needed. Rent a car only for the Rocky Mountain NP day.
guide.stayArea: LoDo or RiNo — both walkable to restaurants and transit, with a livelier bar scene for solo evenings than the suburbs.
food: Avanti Food & Beverage (food hall, good for solo grazing)

deals.whyRanked: $232–259 RT for one of the most walkable historic downtowns in the country, and Congaree National Park is under 2 hours away.
deals.soloWhy: The peninsula is compact, flat, and safe to wander solo end to end, with the Battery, King Street, and the food scene all walkable from a single base.

highlights: The Battery and Rainbow Row
King Street shopping and restaurants
Charleston City Market
Congaree National Park's Boardwalk Loop through old-growth floodplain forest
Waterfront Park's Pineapple Fountain
itinerary: Day 1 — Walk the Battery and Rainbow Row, Charleston City Market, dinner on King Street.
Day 2 — Rent a car, drive to Congaree National Park, walk the 2.6-mile Boardwalk Loop, back for sunset at Waterfront Park.
Day 3 — Historic house museum (Aiken-Rhett or Nathaniel Russell House) and a final stroll through the French Quarter neighborhood, fly home.
guide.gettingAround: The downtown peninsula is entirely walkable; rent a car only for the Congaree day trip and return it same day.
guide.stayArea: French Quarter or South of Broad — both walkable to everything and quieter at night than the market area.
